Thanks for sending the redlines. I've looped in Laura (legal ops) and Aditya (security & infra) to get both the contractual and technical positions aligned. High-level response below and attached a short response doc (RNW_DPA_resp_redlines_v2.docx) with suggested wording.

- Backup/DR carveout: Redwood can accept a limited backup/DR carveout that permits recoverability for operational disaster recovery but must be tightly scoped. Proposed: logical deletion of customer data upon termination and a 90-day window during which encrypted backups may exist for recovery only. After 90 days, Redwood will render data unrecoverable (see Aditya's note on key destruction).

- Irrecoverability timeline: we cannot guarantee instant physical purge of snapshot copies; however, our practiced process is to remove logical access and then rotate/destroy encryption keys which renders data cryptographically inaccessible. We propose the contractable promise of irrecoverability within 90 days, with an exception for court-ordered holds.

- Subprocessors: we will provide the current subprocessor list and agree to 30 days' notice before a subprocessor with access to PII is engaged. For PCI/PHI-level subprocessors we will provide additional attestations.

- EU-US transfers: Redwood uses SCCs for transfers and can act as data exporter for transfer metadata; we'll include the SCC Annex and reference our EU region controls.

- eSign: happy to proceed via DocuSign. Once language is confirmed, we'll send an envelope. Who will be the signatory on your side?

Aditya — can you confirm the key rotation / destruction text below aligns with our ops reality and the 90-day timeline? Ben / Laura / Sofia —

Quick technical clarification to support the legal text:

- Backups: snapshots are stored encrypted-at-rest using customer-segregated KMS keys where applicable. For hosted customers we maintain a split-key model: data is encrypted with a service key plus a customer envelope key derivation.

- Logical deletion vs snapshots: when a deletion request or termination occurs we immediately remove application-level access and mark the customer dataset for deletion. Snapshots retained for DR are retained as encrypted objects. Because of deduplication and immutable snapshot behavior in our storage layer, we cannot guarantee instant erasure of byte-level copies.

- Key destruction approach: to meet an irrecoverability SLA we propose a contract clause that ties the irrecoverability promise to key destruction. Operationally we rotate and zeroize the relevant envelope key within 90 days post-termination, which makes snapshot data cryptographically inaccessible. For customers requiring faster unrecoverability we can discuss a managed bring-your-own-key (BYOK) model with customer-controlled key revocation.

- Legal hold / e-discovery: we recommend an explicit carveout for court-ordered holds; Redwood will preserve relevant artifacts only as necessary and will notify the customer promptly.

If HearthTech is okay with the above mechanics, the 90-day contractual window is feasible. Shortening to 60 days would require operational changes (faster key destruction processes) and an exception for multi-region replication delays.
